title: Rift MCP surface
description: JSON values accepted and returned by the Rift MCP server. Each definition carries the Protobuf identity used after rift-mcp decodes the request.

rift:entryPoints.description: The schema's entry points. Every other definition is reachable from at least one of these seams; shared vocabulary such as SymbolId and Address is deliberately reachable from several.

tree.description: Lists the project tree at one snapshot. Rift derives directories from Git paths and answers without starting a language adapter. A depth of one is an `ls`; an unbounded depth with path selectors is a recursive tree, glob, or file find.

outline.description: Reads the compiler-owned declaration structure of one file. Results preserve source nesting and carry semantic coverage, so an empty outline distinguishes an empty file from an unsupported language.

search.description: Ranked lookup of symbols, leaves and files. A lexical query finds names or text; a structured filter walks compiler facts. Path selectors narrow either form. Every page carries its total order, continuation cursor, and coverage.

match.description: Finds byte ranges. Rift runs literal and regular-expression matching over every UTF-8 file. The owning compiler parses structural patterns because it defines the language's syntax. Every hit carries a key an edit can address.

actions.description: Asks a compiler what it can offer at one address: the fixes and refactors it would suggest there. Each result carries the snapshot and adapter token needed for resolution. Rift refuses a token after its snapshot moves. Call this tool after a diagnostic or before a refactor.

apply.description: Builds, refreshes, or publishes a deterministic candidate. Preview retains each request with its checked preconditions, exact edits, semantic effects, guarantee evidence, diff, validation, and confirmations. Refresh repeats that contract on a newer base. Publish replays it and advances the accepted ref when the retained plan still agrees, fresh validation passes, and the base still matches.

persist.description: Materializes an accepted commit into the session worktree. Each requested path reports its own outcome, so drift, sparse checkout rules, nested repositories, and deletion policy remain visible to the caller.

repository.description: What this workspace can do: which languages have adapters and what each supports, the state answers resolve against, the limits a request has to stay inside, and which conformance tier is in force. Read it before the first call — the tools and resources listed here are the ones this workspace actually serves.

symbol.description: Everything Rift holds about one symbol at one state: the declaration, every leaf that writes it, its types, its edges and its diagnostics. Read it before a rename or a delete, where the references matter as much as the declaration.

diff.description: What changed between two revisions, a page of files at a time: the entry on each side and the edits between them. Git answers it without a compiler, so it works for a language Rift has no adapter for.

file.description: One file at one revision: the entry Git records, its language ownership, and one bounded content range. The next URI continues a large regular file.

preview.description: The complete retained plan behind an apply preview: its input changes, concrete edits, candidate diff, compiler and validator evidence, and confirmations. Read it before publication when the tool result was bounded to a summary.

rift:axes.description: How definitions map to axes. Identifiers are pinned before each group closes over references. For example, `Leaf` can refer to `SymbolId` while the latter stays Semantic. `holds` pins a definition. `residualOf` assigns the unclaimed definitions in one document. The adapter service declares its own groups.

groups.name: MCP

ConformanceProfile.description: Executable runtime claim for this workspace. Profiles accumulate. Every claim validates schemas and examples, checks reference reachability and axis ownership, rejects generated Protobuf drift, compiles the adapter service, and exercises the handshake. Runtime fixtures check ordering, limits, typed failures, the shared-worktree barrier, and topological virtual-source sync. `Contract` identifies the target schema.

rift:enumDescriptions.edit: Adds `apply` preview, refresh, and publish, the preview resource, compiler formatting, and compiler validation. Fixtures exercise every Change variant and advertised action family, complete validation, preview pagination, refresh comparison, rejected-candidate repair, idempotent retry, compare-and-swap races, cancellation, and crash recovery. Caller-supplied validators remain unavailable and `max_validators` is zero.
rift:enumDescriptions.full: Adds sandboxed validators and `persist` materialization. Fixtures verify response preflight before worktree writes, per-path drift outcomes, and shell, network, filesystem, timeout, and output-capture isolation for every sandbox backend. A release claim also runs the suite with two different language adapters and one embedded-language repository.
rift:enumDescriptions.read: Serves the read tools plus repository, symbol, diff, and file resources. Fixtures reconstruct file bytes, verify language summaries and match tags, replay cursors, reject stale state, preserve coverage, and stop at gitlinks. Fixtures cover shared-worktree languages and retained virtual files. Mechanical reads and warm cached semantic reads run with adapters stopped. Fixed repositories record latency, bytes, tokens, and adapter memory.

ConformanceProfile.title: ConformanceProfile

ErrorCause.description: One cause in a failure chain. Entries appear from the outer operation to the concrete failure.

code.description: How this link classifies on its own.

message.description: What happened, for a human reading a log.
message.title: Message

retry.description: What could be done about this cause. The request's outer directive governs the call.

ErrorCause.title: ErrorCause

ErrorCode.description: Why a request failed, as a stable code a caller branches on. The code is the complete classification. Domain results such as unsupported coverage and edit refusal use their typed result values.

rift:enumDescriptions.adapter_protocol_error: An adapter contract is unusable. Causes include a malformed message, a field outside its range, ambiguous source or virtual claims, overlapping write claims, a virtual path collision, and a cycle in virtual-source routing. Correct the adapter configuration before retrying.
rift:enumDescriptions.adapter_timeout: The adapter took the call and did not answer inside its budget. Retrying can work: a cold compiler on a large workspace is slow once and fast afterwards.
rift:enumDescriptions.adapter_unavailable: No adapter is running for the language the request names: none is installed, or the one that was has died. A structural query against a language with no adapter lands here.
rift:enumDescriptions.cancelled: The caller cancelled, or the connection went away before the request finished. Sending it again is fine.
rift:enumDescriptions.content_unavailable: The entry is known but its bytes cannot be produced: an LFS object Rift does not fetch, or a blob the object store cannot read. Retrying does not help.
rift:enumDescriptions.cursor_invalid: The cursor is malformed, or it was minted for a different request, order or page size. Start the query again from its first page.
rift:enumDescriptions.cursor_snapshot_mismatch: The cursor is well-formed but the state it was minted against has moved, so continuing it would splice two different answers together. Start again against the current state.
rift:enumDescriptions.deadline_exceeded: The request ran past its time budget. A smaller one may succeed — a lower `limit`, a narrower path selector — and so may the same one once a cold compiler has warmed up.
rift:enumDescriptions.internal_error: A bug in Rift. `causes` says what it was doing at the time, and a retry is not expected to answer differently.
rift:enumDescriptions.invalid_request: The request does not satisfy the schema, or names something the schema forbids: a `limit` above the advertised maximum, a filter field that does not exist. The same bytes fail identically.
rift:enumDescriptions.limit_exceeded: A request or a response crossed an advertised limit. `limit` says which one and by how much, so the request can be resized and sent again.
rift:enumDescriptions.permission_denied: Host policy refused — a path outside the workspace, a revision this deployment does not expose. The same request fails the same way.
rift:enumDescriptions.record_reclaimed: The record existed and has been vacuumed away after its retention window. It stays distinct from `resource_not_found` because a retry that read a silent miss would re-run work that already happened. Nothing brings it back.
rift:enumDescriptions.resource_not_found: The URI is well-formed and resolves to nothing — no such symbol, no such file at that revision. Retrying does not help.
rift:enumDescriptions.revision_not_accepted: The commit exists, but this session has no accepted publication for it. Publish its preview before asking `persist` to materialize it.
rift:enumDescriptions.sandbox_failure: The sandbox a caller-supplied check runs in could not be created, or died mid-run. One retry is reasonable; a repeat means the host cannot provide the sandbox this profile promised.
rift:enumDescriptions.semantic_snapshot_mismatch: The snapshot passed back is no longer one the server can answer from — the working tree moved under it, or the adapter that held its facts was restarted. Re-read the current snapshot and rebuild whatever was pinned to the old one.
rift:enumDescriptions.semantic_snapshot_unavailable: The revision resolves, but Rift has no index for it yet: the adapters are still analysing, or that state's facts were dropped. Retrying once indexing catches up succeeds.
rift:enumDescriptions.snapshot_not_found: The revision does not resolve here: a deleted branch, a commit never fetched, a working tree that has been removed. Retrying helps only once the revision exists.
rift:enumDescriptions.storage_failure: Rift could not read or write its own state — the semantic database, the git object store, the socket directory. Worth retrying only if the cause was transient, such as a disk that has since been cleared.
rift:enumDescriptions.unsupported_protocol: The client and server use different protocol versions. Compare `Contract` with the client's supported contract.
rift:enumDescriptions.worktree_busy: Another Rift process holds the lease on the working tree this request has to touch. Contention is transient, so the same request retries.

ErrorCode.title: ErrorCode

ErrorData.description: The `data` object on every Rift MCP failure. `code` and `retry` are what a caller branches on, `message` is for a human, and `phase`, `diagnostics`, `limit` and `causes` are the evidence behind the code.

message.description: Human-readable account of the failure. Machine-readable classification remains in the surrounding fields.
message.title: Message

retry.description: What the caller may do next.

at.description: The state this answer was resolved against. Null where the failure happened before one was resolved.

operation.description: Which operation of a multi-operation request failed, as its zero-based index. Null where the request carried one, or failed before any of them ran.
operation.title: Operation

diagnostics.description: What a compiler or a caller-supplied check reported while the request was failing. Empty where neither ran.
diagnostics.title: Diagnostics

limit.description: Which advertised limit was hit, and by how much. Present exactly when `code` is `limit_exceeded`, and forbidden otherwise.

causes.description: What led to this failure, outermost first. A code alone rarely says whether the cause is worth waiting out.
causes.title: Causes

ErrorData.title: ErrorData

ErrorDataPhase.description: How far the request got before it failed. The same code means different things at different phases: `limit_exceeded` while reading is a response too big, and while validating it is a change set too large.

rift:enumDescriptions.discovery: Working out what the workspace can do: capabilities, limits, which languages have adapters.
rift:enumDescriptions.persist: Materializing selected paths from an accepted commit into the session worktree.
rift:enumDescriptions.preview: Building a change into something readable without publishing it.
rift:enumDescriptions.publish: Rerunning a retained preview and advancing the accepted ref through compare-and-swap.
rift:enumDescriptions.read: Fetching what was asked for, from the index, the object store or an adapter.
rift:enumDescriptions.resolve: Turning an address, a cursor or an action key into the concrete thing it names at a state.
rift:enumDescriptions.validate: Checking a proposed change against the schema, the state it was pinned to, and any checks the caller supplied.

ErrorDataPhase.title: ErrorDataPhase

ExactKind.description: An adapter-owned namespaced kind preserving exact language meaning.
ExactKind.title: ExactKind

ExtensionKey.description: A reverse-domain namespaced extension or extension-operation identifier.
ExtensionKey.title: ExtensionKey

ExtensionValue.description: Versioned extension value. data is validated against the schema advertised for its key and version.

version.description: Which version of the key's advertised schema shaped `data`. A consumer skips a value whose version it does not implement.
version.title: Version

data.description: The value itself, shaped by whatever that key and version advertise. Rift carries it and never interprets it.
data.title: Data

ExtensionValue.title: ExtensionValue

Extensions.description: Facts an adapter carries that the model has no field for, under a reverse-domain key. Keys and values use RFC 8785 canonical JSON. `Capabilities.extension_values` advertises every key and version, and consumers skip entries they do not implement.
Extensions.title: Extensions

FactFamily.description: One kind of thing a compiler can tell Rift about a file. Coverage, analysis streaming and invalidation all key on this, so a family is the unit in which an answer can be complete, partial or missing.

rift:enumDescriptions.diagnostics: What the compiler complained about while reading the file.
rift:enumDescriptions.leaves: The nodes of the file's syntax tree, and which symbol each writes.
rift:enumDescriptions.origin_mappings: Relations from produced source ranges to the physical or virtual source ranges that contributed them.
rift:enumDescriptions.relationships: The edges between symbols the compiler read out of this file.
rift:enumDescriptions.symbols: The declarations the compiler resolved in the file.
rift:enumDescriptions.types: The types carried by those symbols. Type facts live in `Symbol.types` and `Signature`; this family records how completely the adapter resolved them.

FactFamily.title: FactFamily

FieldFilter.description: A predicate over a standard, namespaced substrate, or diagnostic field. Rift evaluates the regex operation under `rift-regex`, including filters nested in `StructuralCaptureConstraint.semantic`. Structural patterns and path selectors carry separate grammars.

field.description: Which field to test, by its name in this model: `facets`, `origin.kind`, `severity`. Extension keys and diagnostic fields are addressed the same way.
field.title: Field

value.description: The operand, for every op except `in` and `exists`.
value.title: Value

FieldFilter.title: FieldFilter

FieldFilterOp.description: How the operand is compared against the field. What a comparison means follows the field's type, so ordering ops apply only where the values are ordered.

rift:enumDescriptions.contains: The field holds the operand: a substring of a string, a member of an array such as `facets`.
rift:enumDescriptions.exists: The field is present at all. No operand is read.
rift:enumDescriptions.gt: The field is greater than the operand.
rift:enumDescriptions.gte: The field is greater than or equal to the operand.
rift:enumDescriptions.lt: The field is less than the operand.
rift:enumDescriptions.lte: The field is less than or equal to the operand.
rift:enumDescriptions.ne: The field does not equal the operand.
rift:enumDescriptions.prefix: The field is a string starting with the operand.
rift:enumDescriptions.regex: The field matches the `rift-regex` expression in the operand. Rift evaluates it.

FieldFilterOp.title: FieldFilterOp

File.description: One source entry at a revision: what it is called, what it holds, and which languages read it. Physical entries come from the Git tree. A generated regular entry comes from a retained adapter virtual publication. Bytes are read from the same URI that identifies the entry.

id.description: Project-relative source identity and the URI from which this record and its bytes are read.

languages.description: Distinct languages in `regions`, sorted by language ID. This summary avoids scanning every region. The physical owner reports embedded languages even when another adapter consumes virtual source.
languages.title: Languages

regions.description: Byte ranges parsed with each language grammar. Entries sort by start, end, and language. Regions may overlap when two grammars parse the same bytes.
regions.title: Regions

semantic.description: Whether Rift produced facts from this file. False where there is nothing to read, and where no adapter claims the path.
semantic.title: Semantic

File.title: File

FileChange.description: One file between two states. A creation has no `before`. A deletion has no `after`. A rename has different paths on each side. The path comes from `after.id`, or `before.id` after deletion.

before.description: The entry before the change. Null where the file did not exist.

after.description: The entry after the change. Null where the file was deleted.

edits.description: Text replacements that transform the `before` content into `after`. The surrounding entries carry creation, deletion, and rename state.
edits.title: Edits

truncated.description: Whether edits were dropped to stay inside the size limit.
truncated.title: Truncated

FileChange.title: FileChange

FileContent.description: What the entry holds. Only a regular entry has source in it; the other three are paths that point elsewhere and carry no leaves.
FileContent.title: FileContent

FileContentGitlink.description: A submodule boundary: the parent repository records one child commit at this path. Tree, file, search, and adapter analysis treat the gitlink as one opaque entry and do not descend into the child checkout.

commit.description: The child repository commit stored in the parent tree entry. Its hexadecimal width matches the parent repository's object format. A separate Rift workspace can open the child repository at this commit.

FileContentGitlink.title: FileContentGitlink

FileContentLfsPointer.description: A Git LFS pointer: a stub committed in place of a large file. Rift reads the stub and never fetches what it names, so the size and hash below are the only facts available.

oid.description: The content hash the pointer names. Rift checks the pointer's syntax and never fetches what it points at.
oid.title: Oid

size.description: Size in bytes of the content the pointer names.
size.title: Size

FileContentLfsPointer.title: FileContentLfsPointer

FileContentRegular.description: A physical or virtual file with bytes in it. Every leaf and symbol with readable source comes from this kind.

digest.description: SHA-256 of the bytes. The same value `Snapshot.changes` digests for a file that differs from its base.

executable.description: Whether Git records the executable bit.
executable.title: Executable

FileContentRegular.title: FileContentRegular

FileContentSymlink.description: A symbolic link. The entry is the path it points at, reported as git recorded it, because the target may not exist in this checkout at all.

target.description: The path the link points at, as recorded. Rift does not follow it.
target.title: Target

FileContentSymlink.title: FileContentSymlink

FileId.description: Identity of one file, and the URI that resolves it. The path after `rift://file/` is a `ProjectPath`: unreserved URI characters remain literal, `/` separates segments, and every other UTF-8 byte uses uppercase percent-encoding. Decoding to an absolute path or a `.` or `..` segment is refused. A revision can be attached as `?rev=`.
FileId.title: FileId

FileResourceContent.description: What a read of a `rift://file/…` URI returns.

uri.description: The URI that was read, as it resolved.

FileResourceContent.title: FileResourceContent

FileResourceLink.description: A link to one file at one revision.

type.description: MCP's tag for a link to a resource inside tool output.
type.title: Type

uri.description: The file range to read, optionally pinned to a revision.

name.description: The resource family this link belongs to.
name.title: Name

mimeType.description: What a read of this URI returns: `FileResourcePayload` as JSON.
mimeType.title: Mimetype

FileResourceLink.title: FileResourceLink

FileResourcePayload.description: One bounded byte range from a file at one state. Regular files carry UTF-8 text where the selected bytes form valid UTF-8 and base64 otherwise. `next` continues at `end` until the complete file has been read.
FileResourcePayload.title: FileResourcePayload

FileResourcePayloadBase64.description: A range carried as canonical base64 because its bytes do not form valid UTF-8.
FileResourcePayloadBase64.title: FileResourcePayloadBase64

FileResourcePayloadNone.description: A non-regular tree entry. Its empty interval carries no bytes and has no continuation.
FileResourcePayloadNone.title: FileResourcePayloadNone

FileResourcePayloadUtf8.description: A range whose bytes decode as UTF-8. Start and end fall on UTF-8 code-point boundaries.
FileResourcePayloadUtf8.title: FileResourcePayloadUtf8

FileResourceTemplate.description: The file resource, addressed by a path relative to the project root.

uriTemplate.description: The template, in RFC 6570 form. What follows `?` is optional.
uriTemplate.title: Uritemplate

name.description: The resource family, as `resources/templates/list` advertises it.
name.title: Name

mimeType.description: What a read of a URI from this template returns: `FileResourcePayload` as JSON.
mimeType.title: Mimetype

FileResourceTemplate.title: FileResourceTemplate

FileResourceUri.description: URI for one file content range. `start` and `length` are byte coordinates and appear together. Their absence starts at byte zero with the server's advertised chunk bound.
FileResourceUri.title: FileResourceUri

Filter.description: A recursive typed predicate. Every branch is tagged, so a filter tree parses in one pass.
Filter.title: Filter

FilterAll.description: Conjunction: every member has to hold.

all.description: The filters that must all hold.
all.title: All

FilterAll.title: FilterAll

FilterAny.description: Disjunction: at least one member has to hold.

any.description: The filters, of which one is enough.
any.title: Any

FilterAny.title: FilterAny

FilterField.description: A test on one field of the entity.
FilterField.title: FilterField

FilterRelation.description: A test on the edges the entity has.

relation.description: The edges to look for, and what they must reach.

FilterRelation.title: FilterRelation

FormattingPolicy.description: How formatting participates in a change. The policy is part of the preview identity, so refresh and publish cannot widen its reach.

rift:enumDescriptions.affected_files: Run the language formatter over every text file touched by the change.
rift:enumDescriptions.changed_regions: Run the language formatter over the smallest syntactic regions containing the resolved edits.
rift:enumDescriptions.preserve: Keep every byte outside the resolved edits unchanged.

FormattingPolicy.title: FormattingPolicy

GuaranteeEvidence.description: Evidence establishing an action-advertised or caller-declared guarantee for a resolved change. The record supplies its scope, verifier, method, and findings.

scope.description: Source over which the guarantee holds.

detail.description: Exact property checked and any limit on its interpretation.
detail.title: Detail

diagnostics.description: Findings produced while establishing the guarantee.
diagnostics.title: Diagnostics

GuaranteeEvidence.title: GuaranteeEvidence

rift:enumDescriptions.compiler: The language compiler or resolver checked the transformed program.
rift:enumDescriptions.construction: Rift established the property directly from its closed edit and transaction rules.
rift:enumDescriptions.sandbox: A caller-supplied validator checked the candidate in the execution sandbox.
rift:enumDescriptions.static_analysis: A named language analysis checked a property narrower than compilation.

GuaranteeKind.description: A property an action claims and must establish with scoped evidence when resolved.

rift:enumDescriptions.behavior_checked: A named static analysis or sandbox validator checked a stated behavioral property. The evidence is limited to that named property and scope.
rift:enumDescriptions.bindings_preserved: Unchanged references in scope resolve to the same symbols before and after the action.
rift:enumDescriptions.references_updated: Every resolved reference in scope that should follow the operation now reaches its intended target.
rift:enumDescriptions.syntax_validated: The language parser accepts the affected source under the stated scope.

GuaranteeKind.title: GuaranteeKind

LanguageId.description: A language, as its adapter advertises it. One workspace runs one adapter per language, so this also identifies the adapter that owns a file or minted a fact. Which build of that adapter is answering is on the repository resource, beside the compiler it drives.
LanguageId.title: LanguageId

LanguageRegion.description: A byte range of one file and the language used to parse it. The owner of `App.svelte` can mark its script block as TypeScript. A produced virtual file records ranges in its own byte coordinates.

language.description: The language grammar used for these bytes.

range.description: Offsets of the language region inside the file.

LanguageRegion.title: LanguageRegion

LanguageSupport.description: What Rift can do for one language in this workspace, and which compiler is doing it. An agent uses this to select queries and operations. File recognition, virtual inputs, and compiler write claims remain on the adapter seam.

language.description: Which language this entry answers for. It is the adapter's identity too, since one workspace runs one adapter per language.

compiler.description: The compiler name and version used by this adapter process. It remains fixed for the process lifetime and is reported once with the workspace capabilities.
compiler.title: Compiler

adapter.description: What the adapter build driving that compiler calls itself. Two adapter versions can read one compiler differently, so the pair is what a bug report needs.
adapter.title: Adapter

structural_matching.description: Coverage and failure reason for structural matching in this language. Unsupported coverage distinguishes a missing parser from a complete query with no matches.

actions.description: Coverage and failure reason for compiler action discovery.

action_kinds.description: Supported action families in kind-prefix order. An empty array with complete `actions` coverage means the compiler offers no actions; unsupported coverage means Rift cannot know.
action_kinds.title: Action Kinds

validation.description: Whether the adapter can validate a changed compiler closure completely enough for publication.

formatting.description: Whether the adapter can format changed syntax regions or complete affected files.

LanguageSupport.title: LanguageSupport

Leaf.description: One leaf of a file's concrete syntax tree: the place where a symbol is physically written. It carries where it is — the unit, the byte range, the syntax kind — and the symbol it writes. Everything semantic about that symbol is read from the symbol.

id.description: Unique identifier of this source region, and the URI that resolves it.

symbol.description: The symbol written at this leaf. Absent where a leaf writes no symbol — punctuation, a keyword, a comment.

unit.description: The file the leaf is written in.

language.description: The grammar that produced this leaf. It belongs to the identity because two adapters can produce different trees over the same file bytes.

kind.description: What the node is in its own grammar's words — `rust.fn_item`, `python.call`.

facets.description: Portable structural classification, so a query can ask for bodies or imports without knowing the grammar that produced them.
facets.title: Facets

range.description: The bytes it spans, as offsets into the file.

regions.description: The leaf's named parts, so an operation can rewrite a function body without touching the documentation above it.
regions.title: Regions

parent.description: The region this one is nested inside. Absent at the top level of a unit.

extensions.description: Syntax facts the model has no field for, namespaced by the adapter that emitted them.

Leaf.title: Leaf

LeafFacet.description: Portable structural facets. generated and test are load-bearing: destructive policy, reference policy, and refactor scope all gate on them.

rift:enumDescriptions.annotation: Metadata attached to a declaration: a decorator, an attribute, a Java annotation.
rift:enumDescriptions.argument: A value as written at a call site.
rift:enumDescriptions.block: A run of statements that opens a scope, however the language delimits one.
rift:enumDescriptions.body: The implementation part of a declaration, after its header.
rift:enumDescriptions.comment: Text the compiler ignores. A doc comment carries this too; `RegionRole.documentation` is what ties one to the declaration it describes.
rift:enumDescriptions.declaration: Introduces a name without necessarily giving it a body — a prototype, an `extern` line.
rift:enumDescriptions.definition: Gives a name its body. Where jump-to-definition lands.
rift:enumDescriptions.export: Makes a name visible outside this unit.
rift:enumDescriptions.expression: Something that evaluates to a value.
rift:enumDescriptions.generated: Produced by a tool from something else in the workspace. Destructive policy gates on this, because the next build overwrites whatever you write here.
rift:enumDescriptions.identifier: A name as written, whether it declares or refers.
rift:enumDescriptions.import: Brings a name in from another unit.
rift:enumDescriptions.literal: A value written straight into the source — `42`, `true`.
rift:enumDescriptions.parameter: A parameter as written in a declaration.
rift:enumDescriptions.pattern: A destructuring or matching form: a `match` arm, a binding that pulls fields apart.
rift:enumDescriptions.test: Part of the test suite. Refactor scope gates on this, so a change can be confined to production code or carried across both.
rift:enumDescriptions.type_expression: A type as written, in a position where the language expects one.

LeafFacet.title: LeafFacet

LeafId.description: Identity of one leaf of a file's syntax tree, and the URI that resolves it. `rift://leaf/<language>/<path>@<start>-<end>` carries the canonically percent-encoded `ProjectPath` and the half-open UTF-8 byte range. A revision can be attached as `?rev=`.
LeafId.title: LeafId

LeafRegion.description: One named part of a leaf, and the bytes it spans.

role.description: Which part of the leaf this is.

range.description: Offsets into the file, on the same scale as `Leaf.range`.

LeafRegion.title: LeafRegion

LimitEvidence.description: Which advertised limit a `limit_exceeded` failure hit, and by how much. It is present exactly when the code is `limit_exceeded`; without it, choosing between retrying smaller, falling back to another resource and giving up means reparsing the human message.

field.description: The limit's field name in whichever message `scope` names — `max_page_items`, `max_in_flight_per_workspace`.
field.title: Field

limit.description: The value in force when the request was rejected.
limit.title: Limit

required.description: What the request would have needed. Larger than `limit`, and the difference is what the caller has to close.
required.title: Required

LimitEvidence.title: LimitEvidence

LimitEvidenceScope.description: Which side of the server the limit belongs to. The two fail at different seams: a `driver` limit is host policy the caller can work within, an `adapter` limit is one compiler process running out of room.

rift:enumDescriptions.adapter: A field of the adapter's `AdapterLimits`, advertised in `Describe`.
rift:enumDescriptions.driver: A field of `Limits`, advertised by the repository resource.

LimitEvidenceScope.title: LimitEvidenceScope

Limits.description: The ceilings this server enforces on MCP requests and responses. They come from host policy at launch, so two workspaces running the same Rift can differ. A request over one of them, or a response that would be, fails with `limit_exceeded` carrying `LimitEvidence`.

max_request_bytes.description: Largest request body the server accepts, in bytes. A deep filter tree or a long structural pattern is the usual way to exceed it.
max_request_bytes.title: Max Request Bytes

max_response_bytes.description: Largest serialized tool result or resource page Rift returns. Paginated answers stop before this boundary and provide a cursor; an indivisible result that cannot fit fails with `limit_exceeded`. Conforming `read` implementations advertise at most 65536 bytes, below the truncation boundary of common MCP harnesses.
max_response_bytes.title: Max Response Bytes

max_record_bytes.description: Largest RFC 8785 JSON encoding of one indivisible item in a paginated answer, such as one Change, Edit, diagnostic, or validator result. Resolution fails with `limit_exceeded` before retaining a preview when one item exceeds this value. Host policy sets it at or below 49152 bytes, leaving page space for identity and cursors.
max_record_bytes.title: Max Record Bytes

max_file_chunk_bytes.description: Most source bytes one file resource page carries before UTF-8 or base64 serialization. Rift may return fewer bytes to preserve a UTF-8 boundary and stay within `max_response_bytes`.
max_file_chunk_bytes.title: Max File Chunk Bytes

max_page_items.description: Ceiling on `limit` for every paginated tool. Asking for more is `invalid_request`; asking for less than this still permits a shorter page.
max_page_items.title: Max Page Items

max_relation_depth.description: How far a relationship filter may walk. Transitive callers of a widely used function fan out fast, and this is what stops one query from touching the whole graph.
max_relation_depth.title: Max Relation Depth

max_changes.description: Most top-level `Change` values one preview request accepts.
max_changes.title: Max Changes

max_edits.description: Most concrete `Edit` values one resolved candidate may contain across every change.
max_edits.title: Max Edits

max_validators.description: How many caller-supplied checks may run over one proposed change. Zero where this workspace runs none, which is every profile below `full`.
max_validators.title: Max Validators

max_rewrite_expansions.description: Most concrete edits one atomic `RewriteChange` may produce after matching.
max_rewrite_expansions.title: Max Rewrite Expansions

record_retention_seconds.description: Minimum time Rift retains previews and idempotent publish results after their last access. A later read returns `record_reclaimed` once collection removes the record.
record_retention_seconds.title: Record Retention Seconds

Limits.title: Limits

MatchCardinality.description: How many matches an atomic rewrite accepts. Rift counts against the candidate state at that point in the ordered change list and refuses the whole preview when the count falls outside this interval.

maximum.description: Most matches accepted. Null uses the workspace's `max_rewrite_expansions` limit.
maximum.title: Maximum

MatchCardinality.title: MatchCardinality

MatchHit.description: One match, tagged by the engine that produced it. The tag equals `key.query.kind`. A structural match carries grammar-derived replacement ranges. A text match carries source captures only.
MatchHit.title: MatchHit

MatchHitStructural.description: A structural match with grammar-derived replacement ranges.

kind.description: Tags this as a structural match.
kind.title: Kind

captures.description: The named captures this match bound, in the order the pattern declares them.
captures.title: Captures

explanation.description: Why this is a match, one step per line.
explanation.title: Explanation

replacement_ranges.description: Ranges the adapter says can be replaced whole: the matched node alone, or with the whitespace and punctuation on either side. Rewriting `foo(a, b)` out of a list needs one of the wider ones to avoid leaving a comma behind.

extensions.description: Facts the adapter carries that this model has no field for, under a reverse-domain key.

key.description: Identity of this match and the state it was found in. An edit addressed at it is checked against this before it lands.

MatchHitStructural.title: MatchHitStructural

MatchHitText.description: A text match. Bytes matched bytes, with no tree behind them and nothing to say about what is safe to replace.

kind.description: Tags this as a text match.
kind.title: Kind

captures.description: The named captures this match bound, in the order the pattern declares them.
captures.title: Captures

explanation.description: Why this is a match, one step per line.
explanation.title: Explanation

key.description: Identity of this match and the state it was found in. An edit addressed at it is checked against this before it lands.

MatchHitText.title: MatchHitText

MatchKey.description: Identity of one match: the query that found it, the snapshot it searched, and the range where it landed. The complete query remains available for inspection and replay.

snapshot.description: The snapshot it was found in. A match does not survive into another one, because the bytes its span points at have moved.

span.description: The file and byte range that matched.

query.description: The query that produced this match. One span found by two queries denotes two match identities.

MatchKey.title: MatchKey

MatchParams.description: A match request: the query, a page size, and the revision to run it against. The complete query travels in every match key, so a key can be inspected and replayed without hidden lookup state.

query.description: What to look for, and which engine answers it.

limit.description: Most matches to return in one page, capped by `max_page_items`.
limit.title: Limit

cursor.description: Continues a previous match where its last page ended. Omit it for the first page.
