RepositoryResourceTemplate.description: The repository resource. It takes no path, only an optional revision and cursor.

uriTemplate.description: The template, in RFC 6570 form. What follows `?` is optional.
uriTemplate.title: Uritemplate

name.description: The resource family, as `resources/templates/list` advertises it.
name.title: Name

mimeType.description: What a read of a URI from this template returns: `RepositoryResourcePayload` as JSON.
mimeType.title: Mimetype

RepositoryResourceTemplate.title: RepositoryResourceTemplate

RepositoryResourceUri.description: Paginated workspace metadata and capabilities at one revision.
RepositoryResourceUri.title: RepositoryResourceUri

ResolvedChange.description: Bounded summary of one requested change after resolution. The preview resource pages its exact edits and evidence as records carrying this change index.

index.description: Zero-based position in the ordered request.
index.title: Index

owners.description: Language adapters that contributed to resolution, sorted by language. Empty for a change resolved entirely by Rift.
owners.title: Owners

edit_count.description: Number of concrete Edit records retained for this change.
edit_count.title: Edit Count

precondition_count.description: Number of satisfied preconditions retained for this change.
precondition_count.title: Precondition Count

effect_count.description: Number of semantic effects retained for this change.
effect_count.title: Effect Count

guarantee_count.description: Number of guarantee evidence records retained for this change.
guarantee_count.title: Guarantee Count

coverage.description: How completely Rift and its adapters resolved the request. Publication requires complete coverage.

diagnostic_count.description: Number of resolution diagnostics retained for this change.
diagnostic_count.title: Diagnostic Count

ResolvedChange.title: ResolvedChange

ResourceLink.description: A link to one Rift resource, as MCP carries it. The resource's name and media type are fixed per resource, and the URI is the one that resource accepts.
ResourceLink.title: ResourceLink

ResourceReadParams.description: The URI passed to MCP `resources/read`. Each branch is one advertised Rift resource family.

uri.description: A URI matching one branch of `ResourceTemplate`.
uri.title: Uri

ResourceReadParams.title: ResourceReadParams

ResourceReadResult.description: The result of one MCP resource read. Each Rift resource returns one JSON payload in `text`, identified by `mimeType`. File bytes use UTF-8 or base64.

contents.description: The blocks this read produced. MCP allows several per read; each Rift resource returns one.
contents.title: Contents

ResourceReadResult.title: ResourceReadResult

ResourceTemplate.description: One advertised MCP resource template. uriTemplate, name, and mimeType are correlated per family.
ResourceTemplate.title: ResourceTemplate

ResultOrder.description: The total order a paginated answer comes back in, named in the request so a cursor can be bound to it. Every order ends in the result's own identity, so two results that tie never swap places between pages.

rift:enumDescriptions.identity: By the result's canonical identity: a symbol URI, a file path, or an `ActionKey`. Compiler actions use this order because they carry no relevance score or common source path.
rift:enumDescriptions.path: By the file a result is written in, then its byte range, then identity. Two hits in one file come back in source order.
rift:enumDescriptions.relevance: Highest `score` first, then identity. Scores are comparable across every page of one request and nowhere else.

ResultOrder.title: ResultOrder

RetryDirective.description: Stable retry instruction for one failed request. `deadline_exceeded` can permit the same request; `invalid_request` requires changed input.

rift:enumDescriptions.never: The request fails the same way every time. Change it or give up.
rift:enumDescriptions.refresh_snapshot: The state moved under the request. Re-read the current state, rebuild whatever was pinned to the old one, then ask again.
rift:enumDescriptions.same_idempotency_key: Retry under the operation's existing key. Rift returns the retained outcome when the first call completed before its response was lost.
rift:enumDescriptions.same_request: Send the same bytes again. The cause was transient — a busy working tree, an adapter still starting.

RetryDirective.title: RetryDirective

RevertChange.description: A validated three-way inverse of one commit. Rift computes the difference from `parent` to `revision`, applies its inverse to the candidate state, and refuses overlapping changes it cannot merge without guessing.

kind.description: Tags this as a revision revert.
kind.title: Kind

revision.description: Exact commit whose changes are inverted.

parent.description: Parent against which the commit's change is defined. Required for ordinary and merge commits; null selects the empty tree for a root commit. A commit that does not have this parent is refused.

paths.description: Paths from the original commit eligible for inversion. Excluded paths remain untouched; the commit diff exposes them when the caller needs to inspect the omission.

formatting.description: Formatting applied after the inverse edits resolve.

RevertChange.title: RevertChange

Revision.description:
Which state to answer against. Absent, the default branch at its latest commit.

A git revision parameter, as gitrevisions(7) defines one: `main`, `v1.2.0`, `dae86e1`, `HEAD~3`. Dropping the `/HEAD` from a worktree ref addresses what is on disk there, uncommitted edits included, which gitrevisions cannot spell and is what an agent editing code usually means.
Revision.title: Revision

RewriteChange.description: An atomic query-and-rewrite over the candidate state. Rift finds every match, checks the cardinality, expands the replacement, and either applies all resulting edits or refuses the candidate.

kind.description: Tags this as an atomic match rewrite.
kind.title: Kind

query.description: The text or structural pattern evaluated at this point in the change list.

replacement.description: UTF-8 replacement template. `${NAME}` inserts the source bound by a named or numeric capture, `${0}` inserts the whole match, and `$$` inserts one dollar sign. An absent capture refuses the rewrite.
replacement.title: Replacement

cardinality.description: The accepted number of matches before expansion.

formatting.description: Formatting applied after every replacement resolves.

RewriteChange.title: RewriteChange

RewriteChangeRange.description: Which safe structural range is replaced. Text queries accept `exact` only because they have no grammar-owned trivia boundaries.
RewriteChangeRange.title: RewriteChangeRange

policy.description: Required behavior for every classified remaining use.

scope.description: Source in which complete usage analysis and any requested rewrite may occur.

SafeDeletePolicy.description: How a compiler may eliminate each remaining use while deleting a declaration. `refuse` stops when that use exists, `rewrite` replaces it with a compiler-selected valid form, and `remove` deletes its containing construct at a compiler-selected safe boundary. Complete reference coverage is mandatory; any unresolved use refuses `refactor.safe_delete` before a candidate is built.
SafeDeletePolicy.title: SafeDeletePolicy

SafeDeletePolicyGenerated.description: Disposition for compiler-resolved uses in generated source. Scope must also permit generated files.
SafeDeletePolicyGenerated.title: SafeDeletePolicyGenerated

SafeDeletePolicyImports.description: Disposition for imports, exports, aliases, and re-exports.
SafeDeletePolicyImports.title: SafeDeletePolicyImports

SafeDeletePolicyOther.description: Disposition for complete compiler-resolved uses not covered above.
SafeDeletePolicyOther.title: SafeDeletePolicyOther

SafeDeletePolicyOverrides.description: Disposition for overrides, implementations, and inherited declarations.
SafeDeletePolicyOverrides.title: SafeDeletePolicyOverrides

SafeDeletePolicyReads.description: Disposition for reads, calls, and constructions.
SafeDeletePolicyReads.title: SafeDeletePolicyReads

SafeDeletePolicyStrings.description: Disposition for compiler-classified string references such as reflection names. Unclassified strings are outside the reference set and cannot be claimed by a guarantee.
SafeDeletePolicyStrings.title: SafeDeletePolicyStrings

SafeDeletePolicyWrites.description: Disposition for assignments and other writes.
SafeDeletePolicyWrites.title: SafeDeletePolicyWrites

SandboxedValidator.description: A caller-authorized acceptance check executed directly, without a shell, in a disposable copy of the complete candidate tree. The sandbox denies network access, mounts external dependencies read-only, and discards every write when the check ends.

id.description: Caller label shown with this validator. The result links to the complete declaration by digest, so labels may repeat.
id.title: Id

argv.description: Executable followed by literal arguments. An absolute executable path is refused; a bare name resolves through the sandbox PATH and a relative path resolves below `working_directory`. Rift performs no shell expansion.
argv.title: Argv

working_directory.description: Directory below the project root in which the process starts. The empty path selects the root.

environment.description: Caller-supplied environment additions. Rift supplies a policy-controlled PATH, private HOME and temporary directories, and a UTF-8 locale; it removes host secrets and every other inherited variable.
environment.title: Environment

timeout_ms.description: Wall-clock limit before Rift terminates the process.
timeout_ms.title: Timeout Ms

output_limit_bytes.description: Captured prefix limit for each output stream. `ValidatorOutput.total_bytes` reports the omitted size. The upper bound keeps one escaped validator result inside a 65536-byte preview page.
output_limit_bytes.title: Output Limit Bytes

guarantees.description: Behavior or other properties this command is intended to check. A passing result turns each declaration into `GuaranteeEvidence`; a failed result rejects publication.
guarantees.title: Guarantees

network.description: Network policy enforced by the sandbox.
network.title: Network

SandboxedValidator.title: SandboxedValidator

SandboxedValidatorChangedPaths.description: Whether Rift appends the candidate's changed `ProjectPath` values to `argv` in byte order.
SandboxedValidatorChangedPaths.title: SandboxedValidatorChangedPaths

SandboxedValidatorDeterminism.description: Whether an identical candidate and environment are expected to produce the same result.
SandboxedValidatorDeterminism.title: SandboxedValidatorDeterminism

changes.description: Requested change indexes to which this evidence applies.
changes.title: Changes

kind.description: Guarantee established when the validator passes.

scope.description: Source over which the command checks the property.

detail.description: Exact property the command checks and limits on interpreting a pass.
detail.title: Detail

SandboxedValidatorKind.description: How the caller presents this check.
SandboxedValidatorKind.title: SandboxedValidatorKind

SearchHit.description: One search hit. Its file, leaf, or symbol payload carries the canonical identity.

hit.description: What was found. A symbol, a leaf, or a file — whichever `target` allowed.

score.description: How well this hit matched. Scores are comparable across every page of one request and nowhere else.
score.title: Score

matched_by.description: Which fields produced the match — `name`, `signature`, the text of the file.
matched_by.title: Matched By

relationships.description: Edges from this hit, requested with `include: ["relationships"]`.
relationships.title: Relationships

source.description: The source around the hit, requested with `include: ["source"]`. Carries its span, so an agent can act on what it read without searching for it again.

diagnostics.description: What the compiler reported here, requested with `include: ["diagnostics"]`.
diagnostics.title: Diagnostics

SearchHit.title: SearchHit

SearchHitTarget.description: What a search hit is. Tagged, so the payload correlation survives code generation.
SearchHitTarget.title: SearchHitTarget

SearchHitTargetFile.description: A file hit: one entry of the workspace tree. The only hit that needs no adapter.

target.description: Tags this as a file hit.
target.title: Target

file.description: The tree entry that matched: what it holds, and which languages read it.

SearchHitTargetFile.title: SearchHitTargetFile

SearchHitTargetLeaf.description: A leaf hit: one place in a syntax tree, without the symbol view around it.

target.description: Tags this as a leaf hit.
target.title: Target

leaf.description: The syntax-tree node that matched, and the symbol written at it where there is one.

SearchHitTargetLeaf.title: SearchHitTargetLeaf

SearchHitTargetSymbol.description: A symbol hit: the declaration the compiler resolved, and a link to read the rest of what Rift knows about it.

target.description: Tags this as a symbol hit.
target.title: Target

resource.description: Link to the symbol resource that carries this symbol's leaves and relationships.

SearchHitTargetSymbol.title: SearchHitTargetSymbol

anyOf.description: Satisfied by a text query, with or without a filter alongside it.
Satisfied by a filter alone, for a search with no text to match.

SearchParams.description: What to search for. At least one of `query` and `filter` is required: `query` is lexical, while `filter` is a predicate over compiler facts. `paths` narrows either form before matching.

order.description: Which total order the page comes back in. The cursor is bound to it, so it cannot change between pages of one query.

query.description: Text to match against file contents, symbol names, and rendered signatures. `parse` matches that word in those fields. Caller lookup uses a relationship filter.
query.title: Query

filter.description: A predicate over resolved fields and relationships. This is where compiler knowledge enters a search — implements this trait, called by that function, declared under `src/api`.

paths.description: Files eligible for the search, selected by project-relative Git globs. Omitted selects every visible file.

include.description: Extra payload to attach to every hit. Each entry costs a lookup per hit, so ask for what you will read.
include.title: Include

limit.description: Most hits to return in one page. `max_page_items` from the repository resource caps it, and fewer may come back.
limit.title: Limit

cursor.description: Continues a previous search where its last page ended. Omit it for the first page; everything else in the request has to match what the cursor was minted for.

rev.description: Which revision to answer against. Absent, the default branch at its latest commit.

SearchParams.title: SearchParams

rift:enumDescriptions.diagnostics: What the compiler reported at the hit.
rift:enumDescriptions.relationships: The edges leading out of the hit.
rift:enumDescriptions.signature: The rendered signatures of a symbol hit, filled into `Symbol.signatures`. Nothing to add for a leaf or a file.
rift:enumDescriptions.source: The source around the hit, with the span it was copied from.

SearchParamsTarget.description: Which entity kinds may be returned. Type data is attached to the Symbol and Leaf views that bind it, and filters can search those attachments.

rift:enumDescriptions.all: Every kind above, in one ranked list.
rift:enumDescriptions.file: Entries of the workspace tree. The only target that answers with no adapter installed.
rift:enumDescriptions.leaf: Places in a syntax tree where a symbol is written. One symbol has many.
rift:enumDescriptions.symbol: Declarations the compiler resolved — a function, a class, a trait.

SearchParamsTarget.title: SearchParamsTarget

SearchResult.description: One page of search hits, and what the page is worth. `coverage` is what makes an empty page readable: nothing matched, or Rift could not see far enough to know.

at.description: The snapshot this answer was resolved against. Pass it back as `rev` when a later call has to agree with this one.

coverage.description: How much Rift could see while answering. An empty page means nothing matched only where this is complete.

results.description: The hits on this page, in the order the request asked for.
results.title: Results

next_cursor.description: Pass this back to get the next page. Null on the last one.

SearchResult.title: SearchResult

SemanticCoverage.description: Coverage for every fact family. Absence is authoritative only where state is complete.
SemanticCoverage.title: SemanticCoverage

Severity.description: How much a `Diagnostic` matters, in the compiler's own judgement. Adapters map their compiler's levels onto these four, so a caller can drop everything below `warning` without knowing which language produced it.

rift:enumDescriptions.error: The compiler would not accept the code. Facts read from around it may be missing.
rift:enumDescriptions.hint: A suggestion, usually with a code action behind it.
rift:enumDescriptions.info: Something worth knowing that is not a defect.
rift:enumDescriptions.warning: The code compiles and the compiler thinks it is wrong anyway.

Severity.title: Severity

Signature.description: One callable form of a symbol: the text it renders as, the symbols that text points at, and its structure. Overloads are separate entries.

display.description: The signature as a reader sees it, in the language's own syntax.
examples: def load_config(path: str, *, strict: bool = False) -> Config
display.title: Display

links.description: Symbols named inside `display`, each with the byte range of `display` that names it, so a renderer can turn the rendered text into links.
links.title: Links

language.description: The language whose syntax `display` is written in.

receiver.description: The implicit first parameter — `self`, `this`. Null for a free function, and for languages that have no such thing.

returns.description: What the call yields. An array because a language may return several values, and because a declared and an inferred return are separate bindings.
returns.title: Returns

type_parameters.description: The generic parameters this form declares, each as the symbol that declares it.
type_parameters.title: Type Parameters

throws.description: Types this form declares it can raise.
throws.title: Throws

effects.description: Effect keywords the declaration carries, in the language's own words: `async`, `unsafe`, `pure`. The spelling is preserved and never mapped onto a portable meaning.
effects.title: Effects

extensions.description: Signature facts the model has no field for, namespaced by the adapter that emitted them.

Signature.title: Signature

SignatureChange.description: The desired callable shape for a structured signature action. Existing parameters retain identity through `Parameter.leaf`; a parameter without a leaf is new. Language constructs outside this shape travel in `extensions` under an advertised versioned schema.

receiver.description: Desired implicit receiver, or null for a free callable.

parameters.description: Desired parameters in declaration order. Reordering existing leaves preserves their identity while changing their position.
parameters.title: Parameters

type_parameters.description: Desired existing generic parameters in order. Creating a language-specific generic parameter uses `extensions`.
type_parameters.title: Type Parameters

throws.description: Desired declared error or exception types.
throws.title: Throws

effects.description: Desired language effect keywords, in the adapter's spelling.
effects.title: Effects

SignatureChange.title: SignatureChange

SignatureChangePropagation.description: Declarations and calls the compiler must update with the signature.

rift:enumDescriptions.all: Update the declaration, callers, overrides, and implementations.
rift:enumDescriptions.callers: Update the declaration and every resolved call site.
rift:enumDescriptions.declaration: Change only the selected declaration and refuse when existing uses would become invalid.
rift:enumDescriptions.overrides: Update the declaration and its complete override or implementation family.

SignatureChangePropagation.title: SignatureChangePropagation

SignatureLink.description: One symbol named inside a rendered signature, with the byte range of that rendering which names it.

range.description: Offsets into the rendered string in `Signature.display`.

symbol.description: The symbol that stretch of text names.

SignatureLink.title: SignatureLink

Snapshot.description:
What a `Revision` resolved to, reported beside every answer so a second call can ask the same question again and get the same state.

A commit names its immutable tree. A working-tree snapshot names its base commit and digests the changed set, leaving every unedited file's identity in the base.
Snapshot.title: Snapshot

SnapshotCommit.description: A commit. Nothing about it can change, so the object ID is the whole of the state.

commit.description: The object ID the revision resolved to.

SnapshotCommit.title: SnapshotCommit

SnapshotWorktree.description: A working tree, which changes under you while you read it. It is reported as the commit it sits on plus a digest of what differs, so a second call can tell whether the disk moved.

worktree.description: Which working tree on disk, in the spelling git uses to reach one from another.

base.description: The commit this working tree sits on.

changes.description: What makes this snapshot an identity: two reads of one dirty tree on the same `base` are otherwise indistinguishable. The changed set has no bound. This field is SHA-256 over each differing path with the digest of its content, in RFC 8785 canonical JSON. A clean tree digests the empty set.

SnapshotWorktree.title: SnapshotWorktree

SourceExcerpt.description: A copy of some source, and where it was copied from. A span points into a file that may change under you; an excerpt is the bytes as they were when the answer was produced.

span.description: The file and byte range the text was taken from.

text.description: The source itself, as it stood at the answer's snapshot.
text.title: Text

SourceExcerpt.title: SourceExcerpt

SourceSpan.description: A byte range of one file.

unit.description: Which file the offsets are into.

range.description: The bytes, as offsets into that file.

SourceSpan.title: SourceSpan

StructuralCaptureConstraint.description: A condition one capture of a `StructuralQuery` has to meet. Constraints are where a pattern over syntax reaches the compiler's knowledge: match every call, then keep only the ones whose target carries the `test` facet.

capture.description: Which metavariable of the pattern this constrains, written without the `$`.
capture.title: Capture

exact_kind.description: The syntax kind the captured node has to be, in its grammar's own words.

facet.description: A portable structural facet the captured node has to carry.

text_regex.description: A `rift-regex` expression the capture's text must match. Rift evaluates it with Unicode character classes, linear-time matching, and no look-around or backreferences.
text_regex.title: Text Regex

semantic.description: What has to be true of the symbol written at the capture. The adapter matches syntax; Rift applies this, because only Rift holds the resolved facts.

StructuralCaptureConstraint.title: StructuralCaptureConstraint

StructuralCaptureConstraintCardinality.description: How many nodes the capture binds, which follows the sigil used in the pattern.

rift:enumDescriptions.many: A run of nodes, as `$$$NAME` binds.

StructuralCaptureConstraintCardinality.title: StructuralCaptureConstraintCardinality

StructuralMatchRanges.description: The ranges a replacement can be written over, computed by the adapter that parsed the match. Whether the trivia around a node belongs to the edit depends on what you are doing — deleting a list element has to take a separator with it — and only the grammar knows where that trivia ends.

exact.description: The node itself, with nothing around it. What a replacement in place writes over.

leading.description: The node with the trivia in front of it: the indentation on its line, a separator that precedes it.

trailing.description: The node with what follows it: a trailing comma, the newline that ends its line.

both.description: The node with the trivia on either side. Deleting this leaves no blank line and no orphaned separator.

StructuralMatchRanges.title: StructuralMatchRanges

StructuralQuery.description: A syntax search parsed with the target language's grammar. `$NAME` stands for one node and `$$$NAME` for a run of nodes. Each adapter uses the shared capture, constraint, and result shapes.

version.description: Which revision of the metavariable grammar the pattern is written in.
version.title: Version

language.description: Which grammar parses `pattern`, and so which adapter runs the search.

pattern.description: The pattern, in the target language's own syntax, with metavariables where the shape matters and the text does not.
pattern.title: Pattern

within.description: Optional source boundary for the search. A symbol selects its leaves. A leaf selects its syntax subtree. A span selects its bytes.

constraints.description: Conditions the captures have to meet. The pattern finds a shape; these narrow it to the occurrences you meant.
constraints.title: Constraints

extensions.description: Query fields the model has no place for, namespaced by the adapter that reads them.

StructuralQuery.title: StructuralQuery

StructuralQueryOverlap.description: Which match to keep when one encloses another, as a nested call chain does.

rift:enumDescriptions.all_non_overlapping: Keep every match that does not overlap one already kept.
rift:enumDescriptions.innermost: Keep the enclosed match, and report the chain at its deepest point.
rift:enumDescriptions.outermost: Keep the enclosing match. A chain of nested calls reports once, at the top.

StructuralQueryOverlap.title: StructuralQueryOverlap

StructuralQueryWithin.description: Optional source boundary for the search. A symbol selects its leaves. A leaf selects its syntax subtree. A span selects its bytes.
StructuralQueryWithin.title: StructuralQueryWithin

kind.description: Selects leaf scope.
kind.title: Kind

kind.description: Selects source-range scope.
kind.title: Kind

StructuralQueryWithinSymbol.description: Every leaf that writes one symbol.

kind.description: Selects symbol scope.
kind.title: Kind

StructuralQueryWithinSymbol.title: StructuralQueryWithinSymbol

Symbol.description: Compiler-resolved semantic identity. Source structure lives in Leaf and is connected through Relationship.

id.description: Unique identifier of this symbol across the whole workspace, and the URI that resolves it. Hand it to the symbol resource as it stands.

language.description: The language this symbol belongs to.

name.description: The human-readable name, as written in the source: `parseConfig`. Rendered signatures live in `signatures`.
name.title: Name

kind.description: What this symbol is in its own language's words — `rust.trait`, `typescript.function`. The adapter owns this vocabulary, so each language keeps its own term.

facets.description: Portable classification, so one query can cross languages. `rust.trait` and `typescript.interface` are different kinds that share the `type` facet, which is what lets a search for types find both.
facets.title: Facets

origin.description: Where the symbol comes from: code in this workspace, or a package it depends on.

container.description: The symbol this one is declared inside — the class that owns a method, the module that owns a function. Absent at the top level.

visibility.description: How widely the symbol is visible, in the language's own terms — `public`, `private`, `pub(crate)`. Null where the language has no such concept.
visibility.title: Visibility

types.description: The types this symbol carries, each tagged with the role it plays: a return type, a field type, a bound.
types.title: Types

signatures.description: One entry per callable form. Overloads are separate entries.
signatures.title: Signatures

documentation.description: Doc comments attached to the declaration, with the markup format they were written in.
documentation.title: Documentation

extensions.description: Language-specific facts with no portable equivalent, namespaced by the adapter that emitted them.

document_local.description: Whether language semantics confine this symbol to the document that declares it. The compiler adapter classifies the symbol; Rift does not infer locality from observed references.
document_local.title: Document Local

Symbol.title: Symbol

SymbolFacet.description: One portable category a symbol falls into. Kinds are language-specific; facets are shared, so a filter written once applies to every language an adapter is installed for.

rift:enumDescriptions.callable: Can be called, and so carries at least one `Signature`.
rift:enumDescriptions.extensible: Can be inherited from. A `final` class omits this facet.
rift:enumDescriptions.implementable: Names a contract another type can satisfy: an interface, a trait, a protocol.
rift:enumDescriptions.macro: Expands source at compile time, as `macro_rules!` and preprocessor definitions do.
rift:enumDescriptions.member: Declared inside another symbol — a method, a field, an enum variant.
rift:enumDescriptions.member_container: Can hold members: a class, a struct, an interface.
rift:enumDescriptions.module: A unit the language imports whole. A TypeScript file carries this facet; a Rust module can span several files.
rift:enumDescriptions.namespace: Groups names without being a unit the language loads — a C++ `namespace`, a Rust `mod`.
rift:enumDescriptions.parameter: A parameter of a callable, declared as a symbol of its own so it can be renamed and referred to.
rift:enumDescriptions.test: The language's test tooling collects it as a test: a `#[test]` function, a `describe` block.
rift:enumDescriptions.type: Declares a type. `struct Config` and `interface Props` both qualify, which is what makes one search for types find both.
rift:enumDescriptions.value: Names something that exists while the program runs: a variable, a constant, a function object.

SymbolFacet.title: SymbolFacet

SymbolId.description: Identity of one symbol, and the URI that resolves it: `rift://symbol/<language>/<qualified-name>`. The adapter uses the language's qualified name, percent-encoding UTF-8 bytes outside URI path characters with uppercase hex. Where a namespace declares two identical names, the adapter appends `~` and an index. A revision can be attached as `?rev=`.
SymbolId.title: SymbolId

SymbolOrigin.description: Where this symbol is defined. The origins answer different questions: whether you can edit it, whether it moves when you upgrade something, and whether anything can be read from it at all.
SymbolOrigin.title: SymbolOrigin

SymbolOriginPackage.description: Declared in a dependency. `manager` is the package manager that installed it, so `npm`, `cargo` or `pip`; `name` and `version` are that manager's own. Upgrading the dependency replaces these symbols.

manager.description: The package manager that installed it.
manager.title: Manager

name.description: The package name, as that manager spells it.
name.title: Name

SymbolOriginPackage.title: SymbolOriginPackage

SymbolResourceContent.description: What a read of a `rift://symbol/…` URI returns.

uri.description: The URI that was read, as it resolved.

SymbolResourceContent.title: SymbolResourceContent

SymbolResourceLink.description: A link to the symbol resource, carrying the symbol's own URI.

type.description: MCP's tag for a link to a resource inside tool output.
type.title: Type

uri.description: The symbol to read. Hand it to `resources/read` unchanged.

name.description: The resource family this link belongs to.
name.title: Name

mimeType.description: What a read of this URI returns: `SymbolResourcePayload` as JSON.
mimeType.title: Mimetype

SymbolResourceLink.title: SymbolResourceLink

SymbolResourcePayload.description: JSON payload for one symbol at one snapshot.

uri.description: The symbol this payload answers for, echoed back so a link and its content carry the same address.

at.description: The snapshot this answer was resolved against. Pass it back as `rev` when a later call has to agree with this one.

symbol.description: The declaration itself: its name, its kind in the language's own words, its origin, its types and its signatures.

origin_mappings.description: Relations from produced declaration bytes to source ranges a caller can inspect or edit. Empty for a declaration read directly from physical source.
origin_mappings.title: Origin Mappings

leaves.description: Every place this symbol is written — the declaration and each mention. This is the list a rename has to rewrite.
leaves.title: Leaves

relationships.description: Edges into and out of this symbol, each carrying the leaves the compiler read it from.
relationships.title: Relationships

source.description: The source at each leaf, so the declaration and its call sites can be read without a second round trip.
source.title: Source

diagnostics.description: What the compiler reported at this symbol's leaves.
diagnostics.title: Diagnostics

coverage.description: How complete each fact family is for this symbol. An empty `relationships` means the symbol has no edges only where that family is complete.

next.description: The same symbol URI carrying the cursor for the next page, or null on the last one. Leaves, edges and diagnostics are what page.

SymbolResourcePayload.title: SymbolResourcePayload

SymbolResourceTemplate.description: The symbol resource, addressed by language and the name that language gives the declaration.

uriTemplate.description: The template, in RFC 6570 form. What follows `?` is optional.
uriTemplate.title: Uritemplate

name.description: The resource family, as `resources/templates/list` advertises it.
name.title: Name

mimeType.description: What a read of a URI from this template returns: `SymbolResourcePayload` as JSON.
mimeType.title: Mimetype

SymbolResourceTemplate.title: SymbolResourceTemplate

TextEdit.description: One byte range of one file, and what replaces it. Offsets are into the file as it stands at the pinned snapshot, so edits in a set never observe each other, and two of them may not overlap.

span.description: The file, and the byte range being replaced.

text.description: What the range becomes. Empty deletes it.
text.title: Text

TextEdit.title: TextEdit

TextQuery.description: Literal or regular-expression matching over any UTF-8 file. Rift evaluates this query even when no adapter claims the path. Matches are leftmost-first and non-overlapping. After an empty regular-expression match, scanning advances to the next UTF-8 boundary. The query carries its dialect so a stored match key remains self-contained.

kind.description: Selects Rift's text matcher.
kind.title: Kind

version.description: Version of the query shape and pattern semantics.
version.title: Version

dialect.description: Regular-expression grammar used in `regex` mode. The separate `version` field selects its syntax and match semantics. Version 1 has Unicode character classes, linear-time matching, and no look-around or backreferences. Protocol conformance fixtures define accepted syntax and match selection.
dialect.title: Dialect

pattern.description: Text to find in the selected grammar.
pattern.title: Pattern

case_sensitive.description: Initial case-sensitivity for regular-expression mode. Inline flags may change it within the pattern.
case_sensitive.title: Case Sensitive

multiline.description: Whether `^` and `$` initially match line boundaries in regular-expression mode. Inline flags may change it within the pattern.
multiline.title: Multiline

TextQuery.title: TextQuery

rift:enumDescriptions.literal: Match the pattern bytewise, with no special characters or flags.
rift:enumDescriptions.regex: Read the pattern using the advertised text-matching dialect and the initial flags below.

TextRange.description: Half-open UTF-8 byte offsets over authoritative UTF-8 source. Every adapter converts from its compiler's native offsets at the seam. No JSON Schema keyword can tie one field to another, so that `end` is never below `start` is asserted by the conformance tests instead.

start.description: First byte of the range, counted from the start of the file.
start.title: Start

end.description: One past the last byte. Equal to `start` for an empty range, which is how a position between two bytes is spelled.
end.title: End

TextRange.title: TextRange

TreeParams.description: Selects a portion of the project tree. The root controls hierarchy and `paths` filters the full project-relative path of each descendant.

root.description: Directory whose descendants are listed. The empty path selects the project root; the root entry itself is not returned. A gitlink is a file entry and cannot be used as a directory root.

depth.description: Most directory edges below `root` to include. One lists immediate children; null walks every descendant and relies on pagination and response limits.
depth.title: Depth

paths.description: Git-style include and exclude globs matched against each full project-relative descendant path.

limit.description: Most entries to return in one page. The server may stop earlier to keep the serialized result within `max_response_bytes`.
limit.title: Limit

cursor.description: Continues the same tree walk. Root, depth, paths, revision, and page size remain fixed.

TreeParams.title: TreeParams

TreeResult.description: One page of a project tree, ordered by project-path UTF-8 bytes. A directory precedes a file at the same path, though a valid snapshot normally contains only one.

entries.description: Derived directories and Git entries on this page.
entries.title: Entries

next_cursor.description: Cursor for the next path page, or null after the final entry.

TreeResult.title: TreeResult

TypeBinding.description: One type a symbol carries, together with the role it plays for that symbol.
TypeBinding.title: TypeBinding

TypeBindingRole.description: Why the symbol carries this type. A declared type and an inferred one can both be present and disagree, which is the interesting case.

rift:enumDescriptions.declared: Written in the source by the author.
rift:enumDescriptions.expected: What the surrounding context demands here. A mismatch is reported against this one.
rift:enumDescriptions.inferred: The compiler worked it out; nothing in the source says it.
rift:enumDescriptions.parameter: The type of an argument the callable takes.
rift:enumDescriptions.receiver: The type of the implicit first argument — `self`, `this`.

TypeBindingRole.title: TypeBindingRole

TypeExpression.description: How a type is written in the source, plus the symbol that declares it when one does. A type with a declaration resolves to that symbol; a structural type — `string | null`, `{ a: string }` — has the spelling and nothing to resolve to.

language.description: The language the spelling is in, and so the adapter that produced it.

source.description: The type as it is written: `Optional[Config]`, `&mut [u8]`, `string | null`.
source.title: Source

resolved.description: The symbol that declares this type, where one does. Null for a structural type, which has a spelling and nothing to open.

extensions.description: Type facts the model has no field for, namespaced by the adapter that emitted them.

TypeExpression.title: TypeExpression

ValidationReport.description: One compiler's verdict over a candidate snapshot. `coverage` states how much the compiler checked, while `valid` records whether the checked scope contains an error. Publication requires complete coverage from every adapter that owns an affected file and a valid verdict from each of them.

language.description: The adapter that produced this verdict.

valid.description: Whether this compiler accepted every file in `files` under the reported coverage.
valid.title: Valid

coverage.description: How much of the affected program the compiler checked. Publication refuses partial or unsupported coverage where the change depends on that language.

files.description: Affected files this verdict covers, sorted by project path.
files.title: Files

diagnostics.description: Compiler findings produced while checking the candidate, sorted by file and source range.
diagnostics.title: Diagnostics

ValidationReport.title: ValidationReport

ValidatorOutput.description: A bounded UTF-8 rendering of one process stream. Invalid byte sequences become U+FFFD. The digest covers the complete raw stream, including bytes beyond the captured prefix.

captured_bytes.description: Raw bytes represented by `text` before replacement decoding.
captured_bytes.title: Captured Bytes

total_bytes.description: Raw bytes emitted by the complete stream.
total_bytes.title: Total Bytes

truncated.description: Whether bytes after the captured prefix were omitted from `text`.
truncated.title: Truncated

digest.description: SHA-256 of the complete raw stream. This retains the identity of omitted bytes when `truncated` is true.

ValidatorOutput.title: ValidatorOutput

ValidatorResult.description: The completed outcome of one declared validator. Exit status zero passes. Every other exit status fails. A launch, timeout, sandbox, or capture failure raises `sandbox_failure` before Rift produces candidate evidence.
ValidatorResult.title: ValidatorResult

ValidatorResultFailed.description: A declared validator process that exited with a nonzero status.

declaration_digest.description: SHA-256 of the validator's RFC 8785 canonical JSON declaration. Results and declarations form a bijection on this value, because labels may repeat while commands differ.

files.description: Paths evaluated by the validator, sorted by UTF-8 bytes and without duplicates.
files.title: Files

diagnostics.description: Structured findings produced by the validator. The list is empty when its output has no configured diagnostic decoder.
diagnostics.title: Diagnostics

stdout.description: Bounded standard output from the process.

stderr.description: Bounded standard error from the process.

ValidatorResultFailed.title: ValidatorResultFailed

ValidatorResultPassed.description: A declared validator process that exited with status zero.

declaration_digest.description: SHA-256 of the validator's RFC 8785 canonical JSON declaration. Results and declarations form a bijection on this value, because labels may repeat while commands differ.

files.description: Paths evaluated by the validator, sorted by UTF-8 bytes and without duplicates.
files.title: Files

diagnostics.description: Structured findings produced by the validator. The list is empty when its output has no configured diagnostic decoder.
diagnostics.title: Diagnostics

stdout.description: Bounded standard output from the process.

stderr.description: Bounded standard error from the process.

Worktree.description: A working tree, spelled the way git reaches one from any other: `main-worktree` for the repository's own, and `worktrees/<name>` for a linked one.
